proof:
Source: Simon 7.5.11 and its proof (chapter-07.txt lines 976–1016), Lemma 7.1.4 (lines 62–79), Remark 5.2(‡) (lines 757–765). Departures: [D1] the printed cut-off "ζ = Π φ_j" must be ζ = Π(1 − φ_j) (ζ has to vanish near the singular points); [D2] the printed pointwise bound "|d(ζω) − ζdω| ≤ c|ω|Σσ_j^{n−1}" is replaced by the integrated estimate of step 4, which uses the monotonicity mass bound; [D3] a second cut-off χ separates M₁ from the rest of spt T (needed because ζ only vanishes near sing T).
1. If n = 0 then T = 0 (minimizing 0-currents vanish), reg T = ∅ and the statement is vacuous. Assume n ≥ 1 (then k ≥ 1, as N has dimension n+1). spt T ⊆ closure(E) ∩ U ⊆ N, and ∂T = 0 (T(dω) = ∫_E⟨ddω, ξ_N⟩ = 0).
2. Structure. By 5.2(‡) (Ch. 6, 2.35 in charts of N and De Giorgi's structure theorem, Ch. 3, 4.3), θ = 1 μ_T-a.e. reg T is relatively open in spt T, and every z ∈ reg T has a ball B_r(z) with spt T ∩ B_r(z) = M' ∩ B_r(z) a connected C¹ graph (shrinking the ball of the definition; M' is relatively closed in a neighbourhood of z by properness of the chart). Hence reg T is a locally connected C¹ n-manifold, M₁ is relatively open in spt T, and: (a) closure(M₁) ∖ M₁ ⊆ sing T, and (b) closure(spt T ∖ M₁) ∩ M₁ = ∅ (near z ∈ M₁ all of spt T lies on the connected sheet through z, which lies in M₁). On M₁, H^n(M₁ ∖ M) = 0 and ξ orients T_xM₁ a.e., θ = 1 a.e. Thus T₁ = T⌞M₁ = τ(M₁, 1, ξ) is integer multiplicity, T₂ := T − T₁ = T⌞(U∖M₁) = τ(M∖M₁, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity, and μ_T = μ_{T₁} + μ_{T₂}, so M_W(T₁) + M_W(T₂) = M_W(T) for every open W.
3. Size of the singular set. By the third conjunct (CodimensionOneRegularity) of the sibling dimension_reduction_results: sing T = ∅ if n ≤ 6; sing T ∩ K is finite for compact K ⊂ U if n = 7; μH[n−1](sing T) = 0 if n > 7 (take α = 6). In all cases H^{n−1}(sing T ∩ K) = 0 for compact K ⊂ U (for n = 1, sing T ∩ K = ∅).
4. ∂T₁ = 0 (book (1),(2)). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U), K := spt ω. By the sibling minimizing_implies_stationary and monotonicity (Ch. 4, 3.17) there are C, r₁ > 0 with μ_T(B_r(ξ')) ≤ Cr^n for ξ' ∈ K, r < r₁. Z := closure(M₁) ∩ K ∖ M₁ is compact and ⊆ sing T (2(a)), so H^{n−1}(Z) = 0. Given ε ∈ (0,1), cover Z by finitely many balls B_{σ_j}(ξ_j), ξ_j ∈ Z, σ_j < r₁/2, Σ_j σ_j^{n−1} < ε (for n = 1, Z = ∅). Take φ_j ∈ C^∞_c(B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j); [0,1]), φ_j = 1 on B_{σ_j}(ξ_j), |Dφ_j| ≤ 2/σ_j, and ζ := Π_j(1 − φ_j) [D1]. K₁ := closure(M₁) ∩ spt(ζω) is a compact subset of M₁, so by 2(b) there is χ ∈ C^∞_c(U), χ = 1 near K₁, χ = 0 near closure(spt T ∖ M₁) ∩ spt(ζω) [D3]. Since spt T₁ ⊆ closure(M₁) and spt T₂ ⊆ closure(spt T ∖ M₁): T₁(d(ζω)) = T₁(d(χζω)) = T(d(χζω)) = ∂T(χζω) = 0 (book (2)). Now d(ζω) = dζ ∧ ω + ζ dω and |dζ| ≤ Σ_j |Dφ_j|, so (book lines 1010–1016, [D2]) |T₁(dω)| = |T₁(d((1−ζ)ω))| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ Σ_j (2/σ_j) μ_T(B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j)) + ‖dω‖_∞ Σ_j μ_T(B_{2σ_j}(ξ_j)) ≤ C2^{n+1}(‖ω‖_∞ + ‖dω‖_∞) Σ_j σ_j^{n−1} ≤ C'ε. Letting ε ↓ 0, T₁(dω) = 0. Hence BoundaryVanishes T₁.
5. Minimality (Lemma 1.4, book lines 67–79, in the contract's competitor form; cf. SimonGMT Chapter07.minimizing_summands_source). Let W ⊂⊂ U be open and S an integer multiplicity current with ∂S = ∂T₁ = 0 and spt(S − T₁) a compact subset of U ∩ N ∩ W. Then S + T₂ is integer multiplicity (Ch. 6, 3.2(1)), ∂(S + T₂) = ∂T, and spt((S + T₂) − T) = spt(S − T₁), so minimality of T in N ∩ U gives M_W(T₁) + M_W(T₂) = M_W(T) ≤ M_W(S + T₂) ≤ M_W(S) + M_W(T₂). As M_W(T₂) ≤ M_W(T) < ∞, M_W(T₁) ≤ M_W(S). Together with step 2, T₁ is minimizing in U ∩ N.
key_steps: θ = 1 a.e.; reg T is a C¹ manifold, M₁ is relatively open in spt T and its frontier lies in sing T.
H^{n−1}(sing T ∩ K) = 0 by the CodimensionOneRegularity conjunct of dimension_reduction_results.
Cut-offs around the singular frontier and the monotonicity bound give ∂T₁ = 0.
Mass additivity (Lemma 1.4) transfers minimality to T₁.
